bull.t: Sustained revenue growth and raised guidance
bull.b: A 20-quarter beat-and-raise streak and more than 20% recurring growth excluding political revenue indicate broad commercial momentum. Raised revenue guidance supports confidence that customer adoption, cross-selling, and expanding enterprise relationships can sustain growth over the next several quarters.

bull.t: Strong cash generation and improving profitability
bull.b: Rapid growth in free cash flow alongside expanding adjusted EBITDA demonstrates improving operating leverage and cash conversion as the platform scales. This internally generated liquidity can support product investment, acquisitions, and balance-sheet resilience without relying solely on external financing.

bull.t: AI adoption strengthens platform engagement and retention
bull.b: High Athena usage among superscaled customers, stronger retention from AI adopters, and extensive proprietary data create a reinforcing platform advantage. Deeper AI adoption can increase customer reliance, expand use cases and channels, and support durable revenue growth through higher wallet share.

bear.t: GAAP profitability remains only near break-even
bear.b: Although losses have narrowed substantially, the company has not yet established consistently positive GAAP profitability. Thin operating margins leave earnings sensitive to cost increases and execution variance, limiting the certainty that strong revenue growth will translate into durable bottom-line returns.

bear.t: Channel mix is pressuring gross margins
bear.b: Growth in lower-margin or more service-intensive channel activity can dilute the benefit of platform scale if the mix persists. Margin pressure would constrain operating leverage and require disciplined pricing, channel selection, and execution to preserve the company’s longer-term profitability trajectory.

bear.t: Headline growth includes meaningful M&A contribution
bear.b: The gap between reported and organic growth shows that acquisitions are contributing materially to expansion. Continued reliance on M&A increases integration and capital-allocation demands, while the lower organic rate places greater importance on sustained cross-selling and underlying customer demand.
